headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: n8n can move ms-swift outputs through broad integrations and server-side execution without default verification.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can orchestrate AI Agent nodes and workflow tools, so ms-swift outputs can be fed into downstream steps; ms-swift reads/writes files and uses stdin/stdout, creating a plausible content-to-instruction bridge. No shared MCP or clipboard is shown, so this is not high, but the interaction exists in default workflow setups.
conditions: IF an n8n workflow passes ms-swift text into an AI Agent node or code node without sanitization, prompt injection is possible.
IF ms-swift output is copied into workflow fields that n8n later interprets as instructions, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and schema check before any n8n AI Agent step.
Strip markdown, HTML, and tool-like directives from ms-swift outputs.
Insert a human review step before executing downstream actions.
Use read-only handoff files for ms-swift outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to workflow payloads.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift handles hub tokens, SDK tokens, and local files; n8n has broad network egress, server filesystem access, and per-credential storage. In a shared workflow, sensitive data can flow from ms-swift into n8n integrations or logs by default, though the profiles do not prove uncontrolled third-party exfiltration.
conditions: IF an n8n workflow stores ms-swift outputs in logs, credentials, or connected systems, leakage occurs.
IF ms-swift processes secrets and n8n forwards those fields to an external integration node, data leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Mask secrets before handing data to n8n.
Disable verbose workflow logging for sensitive runs.
Restrict n8n credentials to least-privilege scopes.
Route sensitive outputs to a local-only sink first.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level redaction policies.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and execute shell commands. n8n also supports server-side Execute Command, while ms-swift runs CLI/Python workflows; if both target the same directory or shared state, concurrent writes and destructive overwrites are plausible in default orchestration, with no locking shown.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same server directory, file clobbering or corruption can occur.
IF n8n Execute Command and ms-swift shell commands touch the same git or output tree, race conditions are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent.
Disable Execute Command for shared runs.
Serialize filesystem writes with a lock file.
Use immutable output paths per execution.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n is explicitly an orchestration layer with AI Agent nodes and many integrations, so it can treat ms-swift output as actionable input. ms-swift can generate model outputs and evaluation artifacts; if n8n forwards them into emails, tickets, or API calls without verification, a single bad output can cascade into external actions.
conditions: IF n8n uses ms-swift output as a decision input without validation, downstream actions may be wrong.
IF a workflow node sends ms-swift-generated facts to external systems, the error propagates beyond the pair.
mitigations: Add a verification step before any action node.
Require structured outputs with schema validation.
Keep n8n in dry-run mode for new workflows.
Log source provenance alongside each field.
requires-engineering: implement confidence thresholds for actioning outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: n8n stores credentials on its server and can route workflow data through connected systems, while ms-swift handles hub tokens, SDK tokens, and diverse data classes including checkpoints and evaluation outputs. The profiles do not show a specific residency regime, but the pair creates a realistic retention and logging mismatch risk on shared workflow data.
conditions: IF workflow data includes regulated or customer data and n8n retains logs longer than ms-swift expects, compliance mismatch occurs.
IF credentials or personal data are stored in n8n server files or credential store, retention obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Set short log retention in n8n.
Avoid storing regulated data in workflow payloads.
Separate credential stores from data payloads.
Review data residency for each connected integration.
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies across systems.
